extra_tasks.title: Migrate Ledger to the approved professional UI language
extra_tasks.description:
OBJECTIVE: Apply the operator-approved pilot language to Ledger while retaining accounting-specific density, traceability and workflows.

USER / PROBLEM: Ledger contains equal-weight KPI grids and card-wrapped analytical sections that can obscure financial hierarchy even though accounting workflows must remain precise.

CURRENT-STATE EVIDENCE: Inspect dashboard and representative worklists/reports/forms/details plus accounting-specific states and tests. Preserve all accounting behavior, numbers, report semantics, posting/reconciliation logic and permissions.

REFERENCE-PATTERN EVIDENCE: Use accounting-specific research centered on user financial questions, report selection, summary-to-ledger/source drill-through, table density and traceability.

BUILDING SUIT ADAPTATION: Use approved shared patterns but keep Ledger analytical/dense where appropriate. Do not clone Shop information architecture.
verification_plan: Record accounting-reference evidence and adopted/rejected patterns.
Compare before/after on the same accounting fixture and verify values unchanged.
Run Ledger browser/review checks, app/shared checks and git diff --check.
acceptance_criteria: Ledger Dashboard and representative working pages use approved hierarchy/shared patterns.
Ledger retains accounting-appropriate density and question → summary → source traceability.
Accounting values, posting, reconciliation, reports, permissions, routes and domain behavior are unchanged.
Shop-specific IA is not copied where it does not fit.
Representative rendered Ledger states pass responsive/theme/RTL/accessibility review.

extra_tasks.title: Adopt approved UI PRO patterns in Inventory Suit
extra_tasks.description:
OBJECTIVE: Apply the approved UI PRO methodology to Inventory capability that actually exists at execution time without inventing features for visual completeness.

USER / PROBLEM: Inventory needs to join the Building Suit family without inheriting fake dashboard metrics or another Suit's domain information architecture.

CURRENT-STATE EVIDENCE: Inspect execution-time Inventory requirements, implemented routes/features, shared-shell usage and actual domain capabilities. Identify planned-but-not-implemented features.

REFERENCE-PATTERN EVIDENCE: Use inventory/scanning/replenishment references only for capabilities that are approved and implemented/in scope. Extract action-centric quantity/movement/location/exception patterns where relevant.

BUILDING SUIT ADAPTATION: Use shared shell/archetypes/components while preserving Inventory isolation and domain-specific hierarchy. No speculative UI/backend behavior.
verification_plan: Inspect actual implementation state and record unavailable/planned capability separately.
Render materially changed available screens with representative states.
Run Inventory/shared checks and git diff --check.
acceptance_criteria: Implemented Inventory screens use approved Building Suit UI language and domain-appropriate hierarchy.
No fake metrics, mock workflows or unapproved capabilities are added.
Inventory auth/data isolation, routes and domain behavior remain unchanged.
Reusable presentation remains shared rather than creating a local visual fork.
All materially changed available screens pass responsive/theme/RTL/state review.

extra_tasks.title: Add a bilingual Shop Suit Changelog / What's New page

metadata.reason: Cross-Suit versioned changelog/timeline approved for first launch

extra_tasks.description: Add a customer-facing Changelog / What's New page so users know what changed in each user-visible release. Use a curated versioned source in the Shop repository rather than raw git history. Link it from appropriate app/public navigation. Entries are bilingual, newest-first and safe for customers.
verification_plan: Schema/unit tests for unique IDs, ordering and required EN/AR content.
Route/link/meta and EN/AR responsive browser checks.
acceptance_criteria: Shop Suit has a canonical /changelog (or equivalent) page with no tenant-private data.
Authenticated app includes a clear What's New/Changelog link; marketing/public navigation may link to the same product changelog.
Each entry has stable release/version ID, release date, EN/AR title, summary and user-facing bullets/categories.
Entries are human-curated; raw commit messages, internal task IDs, credentials/security-sensitive details and unreleased work are not automatically published.
Newest releases render first and releases are deep-linkable.
Release checklist requires a changelog entry for user-visible production changes; internal-only maintenance may explicitly skip with rationale.
Validation/tests prevent shipping an entry with only one locale.
Initial backfill uses repository-supported shipped capabilities without inventing unsupported dates/claims.
